ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

schatzker — pattern 5

CT after a road collision demonstrates fractures of both medial and lateral tibial plateaus. Despite the bicondylar articular injury, a portion of the plateau-metaphyseal segment remains in continuity with the diaphysis. There is no complete separation from the shaft. Which Schatzker type best matches the CT description?

  1. Type VI
  2. Type I
  3. Type II
  4. Type III
  5. Type V
Answer and explanation

Type V

Type V: A bicondylar tibial plateau fracture without complete metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation.

Option explanations

Type V: Type V: A bicondylar tibial plateau fracture without complete metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation.

Type VI: Type VI describes a plateau fracture with metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. The case instead matches Type V.

Type I: Type I describes a pure split of the lateral tibial plateau without articular depression. The case instead matches Type V.

Type II: Type II describes a lateral plateau split combined with articular depression. The case instead matches Type V.

Type III: Type III describes a pure depression of the lateral plateau without a lateral cortical split. The case instead matches Type V.
